Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers

card.title: Fermentation to bioremediation — microbes at work

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The same microbes that spoil food serve humanity: Lactobacillus curdles milk (lactic acid), Saccharomyces brews ethanol and leavens dough (CO₂), Penicillium yields penicillin, Aspergillus niger pours citric acid. As biocontrol, Bacillus thuringiensis toxin and baculoviruses kill pests specifically; as biofertilizers, microbes fix nitrogen. Bioremediation lets Pseudomonas digest oil spills; anaerobic digesters turn dung into biogas (methane) plus slurry manure.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: curd: Lactobacillus → lactic acid (pH drop curdles casein)  ·  brewing: C₆H₁₂O₆ →(yeast) 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂  ·  penicillin: Penicillium notatum/chrysogenum  ·  citric acid: Aspergillus niger  ·  biogas: cattle dung →(anaerobic) CH₄ + CO₂ + slurry  ·  Bt toxin: Cry protein vs insect gut

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Fermentations need sterile starter cultures, correct temperature/pH and oxygen control (aerobic for citric acid, anaerobic for ethanol/biogas). Antibiotic production needs strain selection plus downstream purification. Biocontrol specificity is the point (Bt spares non-targets) — broad poisons defeat the purpose.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Toddyinexcess turns to vinegar (Acetobacter oxidises ethanol — same pathway, unwanted). Statins (blood-cholesterol) come from Monascus yeast. Cyclosporin (immunosuppressant) from Trichoderma. Biogas slurry beats raw dung as manure (pathogens digested, nutrients kept).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Trace curd formation: warm milk + Lactobacillus starter → bacteria ferment lactose to lactic acid → pH falls → casein micelles destabilise and coagulate. Every step names microbe, substrate, product and condition — the four-column answer template for all household/industrial items.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Fermentation contamination ruins batches (sterility costs). Antibiotic overuse breeds resistance — production success creates the resistance crisis. Bioremediation is slow and site-specific; heavy metals are immobilised, never destroyed. Biogas needs steady feedstock and temperature.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From metabolism: microbes maximise their own growth; humans harvest the overflow (ethanol, acids, antibiotics as chemical warfare). Match microbe to pathway: lactic-acid bacteria (homofermentative), yeast (alcoholic), Penicillium (secondary metabolites under stress) — product follows lifestyle, so the organism predicts the industry.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Product↔microbe pairs: curd–Lactobacillus, ethanol–yeast, penicillin–Penicillium, citric–Aspergillus, biogas–methanogens, Bt–Bacillus thuringiensis. Biocontrol = living pesticide; biofertilizer = living nutrient; bioremediation = living cleanup.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: curd/bread/beverage fermentation with organisms + reactions; antibiotic and citric-acid industrial sources; Bt/baculovirus biocontrol logic; biogas plant working with labelled flow.
